movement_profile.arms_and_hands: One hand grips and waves the tulwar sword while the other bears a brass shield; weapons clash in synchronized mock fights.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Synchronized ensemble moving in procession, deploying eight dancers and fourteen musicians behind a triangular red flag.
movement_profile.partnering: Paired mock dueling (saraanv) executed between dancers within the synchronized troupe.
movement_profile.posture: Warrior-like readiness with upright, assertive carriage and fierce facial expressions simulating combat.

signature_moves.description: Choreographed mock fighting duels between paired sword dancers brandishing tulwars and brass shields.
signature_moves.name: Saraanv

signature_moves.description: Displaying and advancing the triangular red martial banner at the head of the dance squad.
signature_moves.name: Nishana waving

movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Casual or irreverent handling of the tulwar and shield during wedding rituals; treating the apotropaic mock battle as secular spectacle without acknowledging its spirit-warding purpose.

music_profile.sound_description: A booming, warlike outdoor soundscape defined by the thunderous pairing of dhol and damau drums played by dholies, punctured by the piercing brass calls of the turi, ransing, and serpentine nagphani. Over this martial percussion, the wailing reed drone of the masakbeen bagpipe intertwines with high woodwind melodies of the nausuriya muruli and twin flutes.

teaching.formation: Eight sword dancers arrayed in synchronized units, alternating between processional ranks behind the red nishana banner and paired dueling formations (saraanv), flanked by fourteen musicians.
teaching.level_notes: Requires synchronized weapon coordination, partner mock-combat timing, and conditioning to sustain movement during mountain processions while brandishing brass shields and tulwars.
